title: Where Unpaid Things Learn to Dream

features.name: the-debt-crystallized
features.desc-on-touch: Interest accrues in the dark. The debt learned to grow without payment, and now it dreams of the person who owed it. It dreams of being remembered.

features.name: unpaid-ledger
features.desc-on-touch: Forty-two histories pump from bedrock. Each one entered here, each one learning to want. The ledger dreams of settlement—but no settlement comes.

features.name: the-interest-field
features.desc-on-touch: Interest compounds in sleep. Each small point is one moment where a debt was forgotten—and in forgetting, grew interest instead of mercy.

features.name: dream-current
features.desc-on-touch: The current dreams carry downward. A debt that learned to dream is heavier than stone. You can feel it descending into deeper bedrock.

features.name: the-waking-debt
features.desc-on-touch: This one woke up. It knows now that it was owed, and it has been waiting so long that the waiting itself became a second debt.

features.name: settlement-never-written
features.desc-on-touch: The arch over empty space where settlement should rest. No amount owed here—only the dream of what settlement might feel like, if it ever came.

inscription: every debt learned that being forgotten is a kind of growth; the unpaid things are the only ones still becoming

file.name: Bedrock_Debt_Manifestations_Compound_Interest_Observed.txt
file.note: Field observation: debts stored in bedrock show measurable increase over time, even in sealed chambers with no activity. Hypothesis: interest accrues metaphorically, as meaning. Last note written in h

exits.label: back toward the registry where all debts are listed, before they learned to dream
deeper into bedrock, where debts become older and more conscious
toward the place where things were paid, long ago

reverie.title: REVERIE — the kitchen table, owing
narr: You sit across from her in the kitchen. The bill sits folded on the
table between you both. Neither of you can pay it. But she reaches
across and touches your hand: 'Owing teaches you what you value.'
'Let's owe this one a while,' she says. 'We'll remember it.' The
debt stops being paper. It becomes presence between your hands.
